stimuli.adaptation: Private paraphrase for a concise candidate stimulus; one unsupported added claim about Pip’s local knowledge/ability to escape was removed. Question meanings and answer support must be rederived from this version. Not the original CBSE passage.
stimuli.text: At dusk, Pip is alone in a marsh churchyard near the sea. A rough, frightened-looking man with an iron on his leg seizes him and turns him so Pip must look up helplessly. The man asks about a file and food, then orders Pip to bring both the next morning. Pip is cold, wet, shaking and afraid. The man demands, ‘Tell us your name! Quick! Give it mouth!’ He warns, ‘Keep still, or I’ll make you pay!’

stimuli.source_locator: printed pages 4-5, Q2 informational passage (348 words)
stimuli.adaptation: Private paraphrase shortened for reading-length fit; question meanings and answer support must be rederived from this version. Not the original CBSE passage.
stimuli.text: A survey of 2,000 college students and young professionals examined career aspirations and the influences behind them. Participants represented different genders, economic backgrounds, education levels and career stages so the findings would reflect a broad range of views. Respondents considered corporate jobs, public-service careers, start-ups and family businesses. Corporate work appealed to those seeking stability and structured growth; start-ups and family businesses attracted people valuing autonomy. Preferences varied by region. Participants also reported difficulty finding experienced people to guide career choices. The researchers suggested that later studies could examine gender, emerging industries and technology’s effects on work.
